lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And England wasn't unusual. West Germany's football association banned the women's game in 1955, and only changed its mind in 1970.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In Brazil, a 1941 law barred women from sports considered incompatible with, quote, the conditions of their nature. Football was on the list until 1979.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So several of today's big football nations spent decades actively stopping women from playing. And then, for a while, wondered why the women's game was behind.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Some teams also reported struggling to find decent kit in the right size. The first world championship of women's football, played partly in shirts designed for someone else.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: They beat Germany two one after extra time. For an English crowd, there aren't many better ways to win a final.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: That one was against Spain, on penalties. The same Spain that had beaten them in the World Cup final two years earlier.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Club football is growing too. In 2022, more than ninety-one thousand people watched Barcelona play Wolfsburg at the Camp Nou, a world record for a women's match.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: There is some evidence it works. After the 2023 tournament, more New Zealanders said women's sport was exciting, and viewing of women's sport there rose by twenty-nine percent in a year.
